title: Merge Intervals
contract: Merge overlapping closed intervals [start,end]. Touching endpoints overlap. Return sorted disjoint intervals.
brute: List<int[]> list=new ArrayList<>();for(int[] x:intervals)list.add(x.clone());boolean changed=true;while(changed){changed=false;outer:for(int i=0;i<list.size();i++)for(int j=i+1;j<list.size();j++){int[] a=list.get(i),b=list.get(j);if(a[0]<=b[1]&&b[0]<=a[1]){a[0]=Math.min(a[0],b[0]);a[1]=Math.max(a[1],b[1]);list.remove(j);changed=true;emit("Merge an overlapping pair","intervals",list.toArray(new int[0][]));break outer;}}}list.sort(Comparator.comparingInt(x->x[0]));return list.toArray(new int[0][]);
optimal: Arrays.sort(intervals,Comparator.comparingInt(x->x[0]));List<int[]> out=new ArrayList<>();for(int[] x:intervals){if(out.isEmpty()||out.get(out.size()-1)[1]<x[0])out.add(x.clone());else out.get(out.size()-1)[1]=Math.max(out.get(out.size()-1)[1],x[1]);emit("Compare only with the last merged interval","merged",out.toArray(new int[0][]));}return out.toArray(new int[0][]);
reasoning: Repeatedly merge any overlapping pair until no merge remains; this baseline may rescan all pairs many times.
Sorting by start ensures the next interval can overlap only the last merged result.
Use max for the ending boundary so nested intervals cannot shorten the result. Closed-interval semantics determine whether touching boundaries merge.
